text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation; to begin my assessment, have you experienced any recent head trauma, seizures, or significant changes in your vision?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)

Given your recent use of haloperidol, which can cause muscle rigidity and fever, and your history of tics, these symptoms are highly consistent with NMS. Please confirm if you have noticed increased muscle stiffness or difficulty moving your limbs.
